title: Rebuilding Small Businesses After Disasters Act
official_summary:
Rebuilding Small Businesses After Disasters Act

This bill extends by three years the increased threshold for the minimum major-disaster loan amount for which the Small Business Administration may require collateral. It also requires the Government Accountability Office to report on the performance of such loans.

summary.headline: A 2019 law extends for three years a higher loan-amount threshold above which the Small Business Administration may require collateral on major-disaster loans, and requires a GAO report on those loans.
summary.what_it_does: The law extends by three years an increased threshold for the minimum size of a major-disaster loan for which the Small Business Administration (SBA) may require collateral. Collateral is property a borrower pledges to back a loan. The law also directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to report on how these disaster loans have performed. The official summary does not list the dollar amounts or the exact end date.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that borrow from the SBA after a major disaster
who_it_affects.how: The collateral rules for larger disaster loans stay under the extended threshold for three years instead of reverting to the earlier level.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and homeowners who apply for SBA disaster loans
who_it_affects.how: Whether the SBA can require collateral on a loan depends on the loan amount, so the extended threshold sets which loans can require it.
The GAO report will provide information on how these SBA disaster loans have performed.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 22, 2019. The official summary does not state a separate effective date or the exact date the three-year extension ends.
